results.title: Residents of Waiwayi village in Koko Local Government Area of Kebbi State were seen running for their lives as suspected Lakurawa militants
results.description:
Residents of Waiwayi village in Koko Local Government Area of Kebbi State were seen running for their lives as suspected Lakurawa militants launched a deadly broad daylight attack on civilians. The militants raided Waiwayi, Karwa and Kestu villages around October 26 and 28, burning homes, looting shops and forcing residents to flee toward Koko town. Police confirmed 12 deaths across the attacks, including a police inspector, after joint security teams repelled the assailants.

Videos and local accounts, however, claim up to 20 people were killed in Waiwayi alone, with widespread destruction. The attacks highlight the continuing threat from the group, which is active in Kebbi and Sokoto and carries out raids and cattle rustling, leaving communities gripped by fear.

results.description:
🇳🇬 Armed extremists gun down police officer and dozen residents in Kebbi state attack

Suspected Mamudawa and Lakurawa terrorists have launched deadly attacks on Waiwayi and Kystu communities in Koko/Besse Local Government Area of Kebbi State, leaving at least 12 people dead. Among the casualties is a police inspector who was killed during a firefight with the attackers, while 11 civilians also lost their lives in the coordinated assault. The Kebbi State Police Command confirmed the incident through their spokesperson SP Bashir Usman, though full details about the inspector's identity remain undisclosed pending completion of ongoing investigations into what appears to be another chapter in the region's deteriorating security situation.

results.title: Lakurawa (also spelled that way) predates Tinubu.
results.description: Lakurawa (also spelled that way) predates Tinubu. Local leaders in Sokoto invited the group around 2017-2018 as a self-defence force against bandits. It entered from the Sahel and was initially tolerated. It later radicalised, imposed strict rules, and was designated a terrorist organisation by Nigerian authorities in late 2024. Military operations against it continue.

results.description: Some residents of Jabo, where debris landed, said their area was peaceful with no terrorists. Officials targeted Lakurawa/ISIS camps in Tangaza forests, a known area of activity. Sokoto has dealt with banditry and that group for years, with attacks across most LGAs and over 1,100 kidnappings reported in the year to mid-2026.
